questions.question: Mention the importance of identifying the problem before conducting a sensory test. / [CO3] [1x10 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• Mention the importance of identifying the problem before conducting a sensory test.
  • Answer: The first factor to be considered by panel leader is to identify the problem to be
  • looked into i.e., aim of the test should be known. Since sensory organs are simulated
  • simultaneously, for example, aroma and taste, colour and appearance, etc, the objective of
  • testing has to be clear and focussed. The judge has to look for these attributes only.
  • Identifying the problem helps in selecting the appropriate sensory method, panelists, and
  • evaluation procedure for accurate results.

questions.question: State the effect of temperature on aroma volatility. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• State the effect of temperature on aroma volatility.
  • Answer: The volatility of aromas is related to the temperature of the food. High temperatures
  • tend to volatilise aromatic compounds, making them quite apparent for Judging; cool or cold
  • temperatures inhibit volatilisation.
  • ❖ Increase in temperature increases aroma volatility.
  • ❖ V olatile compounds evaporate more rapidly at higher temperatures.
  • ❖ Aroma perception becomes stronger with increased release of volatile compounds.
  • ❖ Extremely high temperature may destroy delicate aroma compounds.
  • ❖ Low temperature reduces aroma release and sensory perception.

questions.question: Outline the steps involved in conducting a multiple sample difference test / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Outline the steps involved in conducting a multiple sample difference test.
  • Answer: In this test, more than one test variable can be evaluated per session but with
  • reduced reliability. Each panellist is served 3-6 samples depending upon the number of test
  • variables. One sample is a known standard. The panellist compares each coded sample with
  • the known standard. One coded sample is a duplicate of the standard. Whatever score the
  • panellist assigns to the blind standard is subtracted from the score he assigns to the test
  • variables. The panellist is not to guess. Direction and degree of difference is also to be
  • judged.

questions.question: Explain in detail about paired comparison test / [CO2] [10x1 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain in detail about paired comparison test.
  • Answer:
  • The paired comparison test is a discriminative sensory test used to determine whether a
  • difference exists between two samples based on a specific sensory attribute.
  • Principle: Two coded samples are presented to the panelists simultaneously. The panelists
  • compare the samples and select the one with more intensity of a specified attribute or identify
  • the preferred sample.
  • The panel members receive several pairs of samples. These may be different or the same
  • samples in each pair. Samples are always given in code numbers. ➢ Different samples are
  • given in each pair which differ in the intensity of one characteristic, e.g., sweetness, bitterness
  • or rancidity. In each pair, the sample with more or less intense taste will have to be picked
  • out.
